public_rationale: Contemporary generative models could learn from much smaller corpora. Baby Llama supplies a direct example whose teachers also used the small corpus. Leading models did use enormous datasets, but that does not establish the claimed necessity. This verdict depends on reading 'learn' as written; a narrower assertion about matching frontier performance would remain unsettled.
limitations: Baby Llama's evaluations do not establish frontier-level general capability.
The speaker did not define internet-scale or a required level of performance.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Current AI cannot learn without internet-scale data, a flaw of current methods rather than a necessity for AI in general.
conditions: not a logical necessity for any AI

statement.excerpt: It is a particular flaw of current AI — but not a logical necessity for any imaginable AI — that it cannot learn except by downloading internet-sized gobs of content.
statement.document_title: The desperate race to save Generative AI

from_speaker: cannot learn except by downloading internet-sized gobs of content

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that contemporary generative AI requires internet-scale training content to learn useful capabilities. Marcus supplies no frontier-performance benchmark.
A model trained on a substantially smaller corpus is a counterexample only if its learning does not depend on a teacher pretrained on a much larger corpus.

For this ongoing technical observation, the reporting window is the latest completed calendar research year and elapsed days before publication: 2023-01-01 through 2024-01-08. AI research has no standard quarterly reporting period.
The qualification about imaginable AI limits the assertion of necessity; it is not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes that internet-scale content was necessary for useful learning by the contemporary generative methods under discussion, rather than merely documenting its use.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A contemporary generative model demonstrably learns useful capabilities from substantially less data, without inheriting internet-scale pretraining.

evidence.explanation: Baby Llama and its teacher models were trained on the 10-million-word BabyLM corpus. Its language evaluations demonstrate learning with contemporary generative architectures on a bounded corpus, contradicting the unrestricted requirement for internet-scale content.
The section reports training Llama 2 on two trillion tokens. This supports Marcus's concern about the scale used by leading systems, but use does not establish necessity for learning.
